entries.subject: DAMIT 1841: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-1841.txt. Model 1841, version 2017-09-21, pole (108°, 44°), period 13.58364 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 104 ±4 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: DAMIT documentation
entries.finding: [DAMIT documentation](https://damit.cuni.cz/pages/documentation) — coordinate units, pole, period and diameter semantics. CC BY 4.0.

entries.subject: Viikinkoski et al. (2017), Adaptive optics and lightcurve data of asteroids: twenty shape models and information content analysis
entries.finding: [Viikinkoski et al. (2017), Adaptive optics and lightcurve data of asteroids: twenty shape models and information content analysis](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A%26A...607A.117V) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the selected archive model has a physical size calibration. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 104.5 ± 1.37 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 42 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Resolved-model publication supporting DAMIT 1841
entries.finding: The live DAMIT model-to-reference export binds selected model 1841 to Adaptive optics and lightcurve data of asteroids: twenty shape models and information content analysis (2017). That publication supports the selected reconstruction. The imported entry conflated three surveys; listing them together did not establish three usable models or a registered reflectance mosaic.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. 2018
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.06116) and [occultation dimensions](https://www.asteroidoccultation.com/observations/Asteroid_Dimensions_from_Occultations.html) — size comparison candidates; an independent fit or occultation ellipsoid is not silently equated with this mesh’s volume.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: The release supplies no registered surface imagery; the grid marks that gap.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 315, pole ['106', '40'], [Model 315](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/315) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 315: pole (106°, 40°), 13.58364 h, version 2011-04-21, archive diameter 97 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
